messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: High error-rate on serving cluster-gamma — multiple CUDA OOMs + RDMA timeouts detected. Impact: ~15% requests failing, elevated tail latency. Paging @Maya for oncall. :rotating_light:
Maya: on it, grabbing details from console now. which job group?
Diego: looks like gpu-pool-3 (node-45/node-46) seeing heavy IB retransmits. netstat shows repeated RTOs.
Jess: I see repeated container restarts for svc/serve-large on node-45, crash loops with CUDA OOM in the logs. stack: "cudart: out of memory" then SIGABRT.
Maya: copy logs please, Diego/Jess. I'm going to open the incident channel and start a quick triage checklist.
Diego: attaching kernel dmesg snippet: ```[1918300219.345] mlx5_core 0000:81:00.0: Info: IB cq 1234 event CQ_ERR: vendor status 0x7f timeout```
Jess: and the container log: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 6.00 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity)```
Maya: thanks. initial hypothesis: network-level packet loss causing retransmits -> increased tail latency -> KV cache misses and longer seq lengths -> larger memory working sets -> some hosts hit CUDA OOM under load.
Robin: correlating metrics, IB packet retransmit rate spiked at 1918300180 and stayed high for ~30s, then node-45 restarted container at 1918300206.
Talia: Are autoscaler/placement decisions sending large batches to those nodes? Could be bad bin-packing.
Diego: autoscaler did a burst add of pods yesterday. I see heavy co-located big-model pods on node-45 (quantized big-llama). Could be memory pressure + network.
Maya: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon + drain node-45 to stop placing new pods 2) scale down batching on routes that hit node-45 3) route traffic away from cluster-gamma to cluster-beta fallback 4) escalate infra to check IB switch for flaps.
Jess: running commands now: ```kubectl cordon node-45 && kubectl drain node-45 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=120s```
SupportBot: action logged: node-45 cordoned by Jess at 1918300302.
Diego: infra note: switch-shelf-7 shows increased CRC errors on port 12. Opening ticket with DC ops.
Maya: routing change: enabling fallback policy to route /generate-large to model-quant4 on cluster-beta for 10m. Doing gradual shift to avoid a cold-start surge.
Nikhil: FYI model-quant4 has lower VRAM use but slightly different output; will notify product/CS about potential small regressions.
Robin: after drain, container restarts dropped to near zero, retransmits trending down but still above baseline. Node-46 shows small retransmit spikes too.
Maya: can infra run a firmware swap or reset on that switch port? if not, we'll keep draining affected nodes and keep fallback routing until DC ops confirms.
Diego: DC ops says they see a flapping link on leaf-7 port12; they're repositioning traffic and running vendor diagnostics. ETA 15-30m.
Jess: lowered batching config for /generate-large in configmap: ```BATCH_MAX_TOKENS=1024 -> 512; BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=25 -> 15``` applying now.
SupportBot: configmap apply succeeded at 1918300620.
Maya: good. also temporarily lower concurrency for serve-large to avoid memory storms: ```replicas: keep, concurrency: 8 -> 4``` rolling update started.
Robin: customer impact estimate: approx 7 customers with high-volume endpoints hit errors/latency spikes between 1918300180-1918300500. CS alerted and drafting message.
Talia: any sign of model-level memory leak? the OOM backtraces seem instant after GC spikes, not slow leak.
Diego: logs show KV cache miss storms coinciding with retransmits, leads to extra context recompute which ups memory transiently. network seems root cause.
Maya: current status update: node-45 drained, batching/concurrency reduced, fallback routing to cluster-beta in effect. infra running hardware checks. continuing to monitor. last check: error-rate dropped from 15% -> 3% in 10m.
Jess: side note — I saw one container crash with CUDA 11.8 driver complaining about context reset: ```E: GPU:6: Reset detected: reason=MM: Page fault``` Might be driver-level reaction to RDMA faults, worth vendor review.
Diego: opening hardware incident with switch vendor and NIC vendor (Mellanox). adding logs and packet captures.
Maya: tagging CS: @support-team, holding to update customers if error-rate <1% and DC ops confirms stabilization.
SupportBot: CS incident created: INC-7831, assigned to Jess for customer comms.
Robin: infra reports leaf-7 port12 replaced/reprovisioned at 1918301200, CRC errors resolved, retransmit rate back to baseline by 1918301280.
Maya: okay, infra confirmed fix. rolling back fallback routing to normal gradually over next 10 minutes. will keep reduced batching for an hour and then revert if stable.
Nikhil: recommend a post-incident action: add smarter routing to avoid high-memory co-location, and add a check in the autoscaler to avoid scheduling quantized-big and big-llama on same physical host.
Maya: agreed. ACTIONS: (1) Postmortem with timeline and root cause (network flaps -> retransmit -> KV misses -> OOMs) (2) Add autoscaler anti-affinity rule for heavy-model pods (3) Add IB port-level alerting for CRC/CRC-retransmit thresholds (4) Coordinate with vendor for driver investigation.
Jess: handing off to Robin for overnight watch. I'm un-assigning the pager.
Robin: taking over monitoring; will escalate if any regressions. closing active pager but leaving incident open for postmortem.
incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: Active page mitigated; severity downgraded.
Maya: thanks team — great coordination. I'll schedule the postmortem and send notes to leadership and CS.
